intent.goal: Close the sidecar-CREATION race left by #393: a pre-#388 writer that creates and locks <manifest>.lock after the new wrapper's absence check must not silently lose a record. The fix must not create the sidecar and must keep the one lock order.
intent.ruled_out: Creating the sidecar when absent (#388 litter and fingerprint drift; spec scope (a)). Waiting on the sidecar while holding the manifest lock: ABBA against a new writer that joined the sidecar and waits on the manifest (spec scope (b)). Re-checking only right after the manifest lock, the spec's suggested point: that leaves the read, parse and serialize inside the residual gap, and the pre-truncate look already covers every sidecar that appears earlier, since legacy writers never remove theirs. A post-write verify-and-reappend: it needs a record identity the ledger lacks (two same-second runs of one command write byte-identical records), adds a second retry loop, and only narrows a gap that is already a few syscalls wide. Accept-with-reason alone (coordinator-declined in the spec). Lock-free peers (impossible, spec scope note).
intent.why: Legacy writers go create -> lock -> read -> write, and never remove the sidecar (e04b0c2 opens it 'a' and leaves it). So if no sidecar exists at the moment just before this append truncates, no legacy writer has read the manifest yet, and if one exists, rejoining it waits out any legacy read-modify-write in flight. Looking as late as possible makes the unguarded span the smallest it can be without creating the file: a seek, a truncate and the payload's buffered write, whose last bytes reach the file only as the `with` closes it. The rejoin reuses sidecar_lock and the existing `with`, so the lock order holds by construction.

noticed_not_touched: RESIDUAL (disclosed, not closed): a legacy writer can still create the sidecar, lock it and start its cycle between this append's last look and the close that flushes its write (a seek, a truncate and the payload's buffered write). The outcome turns on where the legacy steps land. (1) Its whole cycle before the truncate: this write replaces its rewrite, and the legacy record is dropped with no warning. (2) Its read before the truncate, its rewrite after the close: that rewrite replaces this one, and this record is dropped with no warning. (3) Its read before the truncate, its rewrite between the truncate and the flush: the flush writes this payload over it from offset 0, and when the legacy rewrite is the longer its tail survives past this JSON. The manifest no longer parses ('Extra data'), the tearing append warns nothing, and every later append, of either version, warns and records nothing until the file is repaired by hand: the ledger is poisoned. (4) Its read inside the gap: it cannot parse the empty or partly flushed file, so it warns and drops its own record. All four are forced through the real append_record in u393r-negctrl.txt ROUND 3 (the tear: 'Extra data: line 13 column 1 (char 108)', the tearing append's stderr empty, three later appends each WARNING with the manifest unchanged). Second loss path: the last attempt writes even when its look finds a sidecar it did not join (REJOIN_ATTEMPTS). A legacy writer holding that sidecar can then overlap the whole attempt, not just the gap, with the same outcomes. That needs the sidecar deleted and recreated between attempts, which a legacy writer never does. Closing the window needs the new wrapper to create the sidecar, which #388 forbids. It is unforced-unreachable in practice (the wider pre-fix window already showed 0/60 unforced). V393R-r1 accepted it with reason (Greptile P1 4015794383); V393R-r2 kept that acceptance and asked only that the outcomes be named.

A sidecar that appears mid-append and cannot be opened (EACCES, a directory) now makes the rejoin's open raise OSError: WARNING, record not written, exit code unchanged. That is the same handling U393 gives a pre-existing unopenable sidecar. A legacy writer creates it 0666 & umask, so this needs a hostile or broken peer. No test pins it.

The rejoin waits on the sidecar without a bound, as the U393 join and the manifest lock already do: a hung legacy holder stalls the wrapper after the child has exited (the exit code is already fixed). Unchanged in kind from base.
Lock-free peers stay out of scope (spec scope note). The in-place truncate+write is still not atomic for LOCK-FREE readers such as verify.py; unchanged from base.

REJOIN_ATTEMPTS = 3: legacy writers never remove the sidecar, so the second attempt holds it. The bound only matters if a third party deletes and recreates the file, and the last attempt writes regardless, per the spec's 'bounded retries, then proceed'.

RESIDUAL window, stated for adjudication: see noticed_not_touched[0] and the append_record docstring. The builder judges it acceptable: the gap is a few syscalls wide, it cannot be closed under #388, and C-1's forced schedule, the natural shape of the race, is closed.
